description: IDDFS (iterative deepening depth-first search) finds a path with the fewest edges, in memory linear in that path's length. It ignores edge costs, so the path is not always the cheapest one. It runs a depth-limited depth-first search with the limits 0, 1, 2, and so on, until a search finds a goal; if a limit cuts off nothing, no goal is reachable and IDDFS reports failure. It keeps only the current path, so it skips cycles on that path but can visit a state many times along different paths and in every iteration. Use it when breadth-first search would need too much memory and the solution is shallow.

papers.title: Depth-first iterative-deepening: An optimal admissible tree search

lineage.source: heuristic-search, src/depth_first.rs: "Runs depth_limited_dfs with limits 0, 1, 2, ... until a goal is found or a limit cuts nothing off"
